slides.headline: Just women spinning wool? The real story is at the back.
The workshop
slides.text: At first it looks like an ordinary workshop in Madrid: women spinning wool, a cat, balls of thread on the floor.

slides.headline: The wheel
slides.text: On the left, an older woman turns the spinning wheel so fast that its spokes have vanished into a blur.

slides.headline: The young one
slides.text: On the right, a young woman winds yarn with her back to us, caught in a bright beam of light.

slides.headline: The back room
slides.text: But the real story is in the bright room at the back. Elegant ladies stand there in front of a tapestry.

slides.headline: The goddess
slides.text: One of them wears a helmet: she is Athena, goddess of weaving. She has come to judge a contest.

slides.headline: Arachne
slides.text: Arachne, a young weaver, boasted that she was better than the goddess. Her tapestry showed the gods behaving badly.

slides.headline: The punishment
slides.text: In the myth, Athena turns Arachne into a spider, weaving forever. That is why spiders are still called arachnids.

slides.headline: Talent or pride?
slides.text: Velázquez hid a myth behind a workshop. Was Arachne right to challenge a goddess, if she really was the best?
